extracted.intended_audience: federal agency rule drafters, regulations counsel, and Office of the Federal Register submitters
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for preparing agency documents for publication in the Federal Register and codification in the Code of Federal Regulations, including document structure, citations, headings, incorporation by reference, and procedural submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must comply with the deadline dates established by the Director of the Federal Register for transmittal of statements and the verification of proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Manual is published on a schedule to provide timely information; failure to comply may result in publication of an outdated statement or omission of important material, depriving the public of expected information in a particular edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting (§ 21.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency that prepares a document subject to codification shall draft it as an amendment to the Code of Federal Regulations in accordance with this subchapter before submitting it to the Office of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents must be prepared as CFR amendments and follow the provisions of the subchapter; see also requirement to include words of issuance and amendatory language that precisely describes the relationship of new provisions to the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words of issuance and amendatory language
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall include words of issuance and amendatory language that precisely describes the relationship of the new provisions to the Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language must clearly and precisely identify how new provisions change or relate to the CFR (e.g., stating whether language replaces, adds, or removes sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of expiration of codified material (§ 21.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a codified regulation expires after a specified period by its own terms or by law, the issuing agency shall submit a notification by document for publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must publish notifications of expirations so the Code accurately reflects material in force or expired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles and subtitles (§ 21.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The major divisions of the Code are titles; subtitles may be used to distinguish between materials from an overall agency and materials issued by components or to group chapters within a title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use titles for broadly related Government functions; use subtitles when appropriate to separate agency components or group chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapters and subchapters (§ 21.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Normal divisions of a title are chapters (assigned to agencies) and subchapters may be used to group related parts within a chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter and subchapter assignments are made by the Office of the Federal Register after agency consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts, subparts, and undesignated center heads (§ 21.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts are the normal divisions of a chapter (unified body of regulations); subparts or undesignated center heads may group related sections within a part or subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subparts or center heads to group related sections; undesignated center heads may group sections within a subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections and internal divisions (§ 21.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections are the basic units of the Code; when internal division is necessary, sections may be divided into paragraphs, which may be further subdivided using specified lettering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections precede paragraphing; follow the paragraph-level designations in § 21.11(h) for consistent subdivision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard organization and numbering (§ 21.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard organization consists of titles (Arabic), subtitles (capital letters), chapters (Roman capitals), subchapters (capital letters), parts (Arabic), subparts (capital letters), sections (Arabic within each part), and paragraph level designations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: section number includes part number and section (e.g., § 21.15). Paragraph level designations are: (a),(b),(c)...; (1),(2),(3)...; (i),(ii),(iii)...; (A),(B),(C)...; (1),(2),(3)...; (i),(ii),(iii).... Follow these conventions for uniformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation of numbers (§ 21.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where related parts or sections are grouped under a heading, numbers may be reserved at the end of each group to allow for expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve numbers to permit future additions without renumbering existing material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviations from standard organization (§ 21.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any deviation from standard CFR designations must be approved in advance by the Office of the Federal Register; requests must be submitted in writing at least five working days before final rule submission and include a copy of the final rule document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may allow special keying of section numbers to correspond to an agency system only when it benefits both the agency and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document headings (§ 21.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rule and proposed rule document submitted shall contain the following headings, when appropriate, on separate lines in the following order: (1) Agency name; (2) Subagency name; (3) Numerical references to the CFR title and parts affected; (4) Agency numbers or identifying symbol in brackets, if used; (5) Brief subject heading describing the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each CFR section must also have a brief descriptive heading preceding the text on a separate line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables of contents (§ 21.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: A table of contents shall be used at the beginning of the part whenever a new part is introduced, an existing part is completely revised, or a group of sections is revised/added and set forth as a subpart or grouped under a center head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table shall follow the part heading, precede the regulatory text, and list headings for subparts, center headings, sections, and appendix headings to the part or subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of part headings (§ 21.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each part heading shall indicate briefly the general subject matter of the part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use non-descriptive phrases such as 'Regulations under the Act of July 28, 1955' or introductory expressions like 'Regulations governing' or 'Rules applicable to'—headings must be descriptive of subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments: identification and format (§ 21.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each amendatory document shall identify in specific terms the unit amended and the extent of the changes made; the number and heading of each section amended shall be set forth in full on a separate line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about what is amended and show section numbers and headings in full to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: References: specificity and publication (§ 21.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each reference to the Code of Federal Regulations shall be in terms of the specific titles, chapters, parts, sections, and paragraphs involved; ambiguous references such as 'herein', 'above', 'below' may not be used. Each document that contains a reference to material published in the Code shall include the Code citation as part of the reference. Each agency shall publish its own regulations in full text; cross-references to another agency's regulations may not be used as a substitute unless exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed exceptions where cross-references are acceptable: (1) required by court order, statute, Executive order, or reorganization plan; (2) reference to regulations of an agency with exclusive legal authority where referencing agency needs to apply them; (3) references that are informational or improve clarity rather than being regulatory; (4) references to Federal agency test methods or consensus standards that have replaced private standards; (5) references from subagency to Department level. Use explicit CFR citations in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel citations of Code and Federal Register (§ 21.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: For parallel reference, the Code of Federal Regulations and the FEDERAL REGISTER may be cited in specified forms, e.g., 'lll CFR lll (lll FR lll).' or '§ lll of this chapter (lll FR lll).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the appropriate parallel citation forms when citing both CFR and FR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date statement (§ 21.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document subject to codification shall include a clear statement as to the date or dates upon which its contents become effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State effective dates precisely in the document to avoid confusion about enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB control numbers (§ 21.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: To display OMB control numbers in agency regulations, those numbers shall be placed parenthetically at the end of the section or displayed in a table or codified section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure OMB control numbers are shown consistently and clearly for information collection approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: General requirements: authority citations (§ 21.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section in a document subject to codification must include, or be covered by, a complete citation of the authority under which the section is issued, including (a) general or specific authority delegated by statute; and (b) executive delegations, if any, necessary to link the statutory authority to the issuing agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority citations must fully identify statutory and executive delegation bases for regulatory issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency responsibility for authority citations (§ 21.41)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each issuing agency is responsible for the accuracy and integrity of the citations of authority in the documents it issues and shall formally amend citations in its codified material to reflect any changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must proactively update authority citations when statutory or delegation changes occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to citation placement/form (§ 21.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register may make exceptions to requirements relating to placement and form of citations of authority whenever strict application would impair practical use of the citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek Director approval when strict adherence would reduce practical utility; document the rationale if exception is sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placing and amending authority citations (§ 21.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for placing authority citations vary with amendment type: if document sets out an entire CFR part, place complete authority citation after table of contents and before regulatory text; if amending only certain sections, present complete authority citation to the part as first item in list of amendments; centralized authority citation should appear at end of the table of contents for a part or after each subpart heading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the authority for an amendment is the same as the part, restate it; if it changes, revise the authority citation in its entirety and specify particular authorities for certain sections as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory authority placement (§ 21.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation to a nonstatutory document as authority shall be placed after the statutory citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List statutory citations first, then nonstatutory sources (e.g., E.O.s, regulations, special civil air regs) with appropriate formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of authority citations (§ 21.51)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal citations of authority shall be in the shortest form compatible with positive identification and ready reference; the Office of the Federal Register will assist agencies in developing model citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep citations concise but uniquely identifiable; consult OFR for model language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory material citation rules (§ 21.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: All citations to statutory authority shall include a United States Code citation, where available; citations to titles of the U.S. Code may be cited without Public Law or U.S. Statutes at Large citation. Citations to Public Laws and U.S. Statutes at Large are optional when the U.S. Code is cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'AUTHORITY: 10 U.S.C. 501.' When citing Statutes at Large, refer to the section of the public law and volume/page where section begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory materials citation rules (§ 21.53)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonstatutory documents shall be cited by document designation and by FEDERAL REGISTER volume and page, followed, if possible, by the parallel citation to the Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide FR volume/page and any parallel CFR citation to aid identification (example formats provided in the section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Name of issuing agency and subdivision (Part 22, § 22.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the agency issuing a notice shall be placed at the beginning of the document; if a specific bureau/service issues the notice, its name shall be on a separate line below the agency name; file numbers/docket numbers should be placed in brackets immediately below the other headings; a suitable short title identifying the subject shall be provided on a separate line immediately after other required captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a brief additional caption indicating nature of the document when appropriate; use bracketed identifiers for docket/file numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citation for notices (§ 22.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority under which an agency issues a notice shall be cited in narrative form within text or in parentheses on a separate line following text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite statutory or other authority clearly in notices so readers understand the legal basis for the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed rule general requirements (§ 22.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposed rule required by section 553 of title 5 U.S.C., or any similar document, shall include a statement of (a) the time, place, and nature of public rulemaking proceedings; and (b) reference to the authority under which the regulatory action is proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure public participation logistics and statutory authority are stated in the proposed rule preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code designation in proposed rules (§ 22.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The area of the Code of Federal Regulations directly affected by a proposed regulatory action shall be identified by placing the appropriate CFR citation immediately below the name of the issuing agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the CFR citation conspicuously (immediately below agency name) to show which parts/sections are affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codification conformity for proposed rules (§ 22.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any part of a proposed rule document that contains the full text of a proposed regulation shall also conform to the pertinent provisions of part 21 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If including full regulatory text in the proposal, follow part 21 formatting, headings, numbering, and other codification rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on incorporation by reference (§ 51.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation by reference is governed by 5 U.S.C. 552(a): matter reasonably available to the class of persons affected is deemed published in the Federal Register when incorporated by reference with Director approval; the Director will interpret 552(a) together with other publication requirements and will assume incorporation is intended to benefit both government and affected persons and not detract from legal/practical attributes of publication systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation is limited to the approved edition; future amendments or revisions of the publication are not included unless separately approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: When the Director will approve a publication (§ 51.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will approve incorporation by reference when: (1) the publication is eligible (§ 51.7); (2) the language of incorporation meets this part (§ 51.9); (3) the publication is on file with the Office of the Federal Register; and (4) the Director has received a written request from the agency to approve the incorporation by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director will notify the agency of approval or disapproval within 20 working days after requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: How an agency requests approval (§ 51.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal approval applies to a final rule document; for timely approval the agency must: (1) make a written request at least 20 working days before submitting the final rule document; (2) send with the request a copy of the final rule document that uses proper language of incorporation; and (3) ensure a copy of the publication is on file at the Office of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may consult with the Office of the Federal Register at any time regarding requirements; follow the 20-working-day timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for incorporation by reference (§ 51.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A publication is eligible if it: (1) conforms to the policy in § 51.1; (2) is published data, criteria, standards, specifications, techniques, illustrations, or similar material; (3) substantially reduces the volume of material published in the FEDERAL REGISTER; and (4) is reasonably available to and usable by the class of persons affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining usability, Director will consider completeness and ease of handling, and whether it is bound, numbered, and organized. Publications produced by the same agency are presumed inappropriate unless judged unique or cannot be printed by FR/CFR printing system. Materials not appropriate: (1) material previously published in the FEDERAL REGISTER; (2) material published in the United States Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper language of incorporation (§ 51.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Language incorporating a publication by reference shall be as precise and complete as possible and shall make clear that the incorporation is intended and completed by the final rule document in which it appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language is precise if it: (1) uses the words 'incorporated by reference'; (2) states title, date, edition, author, publisher, and identification number; (3) informs the user that the incorporated publication is a requirement; (4) makes an official showing where/how copies may be examined and readily obtained; and (5) refers to 5 U.S.C. 552(a). If approved, the agency must include a statement under the DATES caption that incorporation is approved by the Director as of [date], and include the term 'incorporation by reference' in index terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing or removing an approved incorporation (§ 51.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency seeking approval for a change to an incorporated publication must: (1) publish notice of the change in the FEDERAL REGISTER and amend the CFR; (2) ensure a copy of the amendment/revision is on file at the Office of the Federal Register; and (3) notify the Director in writing that the change is being made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a regulation containing an incorporation fails to become effective or is removed from the CFR, the agency must notify the Director in writing within 5 working days of the occurrence.
